welcome.title: 🧾 Your business’s receipt
welcome.description:
Here you decide what prints when you charge someone: your logo, your name, a thank-you at the end.

Whatever you build here gets printed by all your devices, without touching a single one.

open.title: Open the designer
open.description: You’ll see two things at once: the list of what your receipt includes on the left, and the actual receipt on the right.

list.title: The list: what your receipt includes
list.description:
Each row is a piece of the receipt, and they print in this order.

The arrows move a piece up and down. The ✕ removes it. The paper on the right updates instantly, so you never save blind.

locks.title: 🔒 Why some pieces can’t be removed
locks.description:
Some carry a lock: they can be moved, but not removed. The letter says why, and there are three different reasons:

• L — the law requires it (your tax ID, the items, the total)
• O — your operation needs it (the payment, the pickup stub)
• P — it belongs to Avoqado

Hover over it and it tells you.

paper.title: The paper, at real size
paper.description:
This is not a rough sketch: it’s the same receipt that will come out of your printer, with the same width and the same line breaks.

If a text doesn’t fit, you’ll see it cut off here — before printing a thousand.

width.title: The two paper widths
width.description:
80 mm paper fits 48 characters per line; 58 mm fits only 32.

If you use both sizes, check both: a text that fits the wide one gets cut on the narrow one.

save.title: Save
save.description:
Once you save, your devices pick up the new design on their own.

If someone else on your team changed it while you were editing, we tell you their name instead of overwriting their work.

And if you don’t like the result, “Reset” takes you back to Avoqado’s receipt.
